title: Unique normalized scalar and pullback comparisons on quotient cochains
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$. For every finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and scheme $W$, use the quotient coefficient sequence ring sheaf and its module category [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Let $T_{E,W}$ be signed direct-sum total tensor on integer cochain complexes of these modules [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every finite coefficient homomorphism $i:E\to L$, let $S_i$ be termwise extension of scalars; for every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, let $F_E$ be the termwise sequence-site module pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is exactly one pair of families of natural isomorphisms $\sigma:T_{E,W}S_i\simeq(S_i,S_i)T_{L,W}$ and $c:T_{E,Y}F_E\simeq(F_E,F_E)T_{E,X}$ such that on every local homogeneous tensor the scalar map sends $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ and the pullback map sends $b\cdot u(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\cdot u(x))\otimes u(y)$, where $u$ denotes the pullback adjunction unit. All natural transformations are maps on the whole sequence site, retaining quotient transitions. Equivalently, the type Comparisons of [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data] with these formulas has a Unique structure.

proof.text: Specialize the existing sheaf scalar total-tensor comparison to the coefficient-sequence ring map. Its formula at coefficient one extends to arbitrary coefficients by scalar linearity and balancing. The normalized cochain pullback/tensor comparison supplies the pullback family. These give the two maps and their required formulas. For uniqueness transpose the scalar map through its extension/restriction adjunction, and transpose the pullback map through the geometric pullback/direct-image adjunction. Homogeneous tensor generators determine each degreewise map, hence both natural isomorphisms. Proof irrelevance identifies their formula fields. Thus the existing ComparisonData record has exactly one inhabitant. Inverses and all quotient restrictions are retained because every map is a natural transformation on the sequence site.
